output.text: TypeScript is a strongly typed programming language that builds on JavaScript, adding optional static typing, generics, and tooling. Sources: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/intro.html and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TypeScript

input.query: What is the weather in Quito?

output.text: Current weather information for Quito: a mild highland climate around 13-19 degrees Celsius with intermittent rain and strong UV at altitude. Sources: https://weather.com/weather/today and https://worldweatheronline.com/quito

Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI agents: it provides agents, workflows, RAG, evals, and observability, deployable anywhere Node runs. Sources: https://mastra.ai/docs and https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra

Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) grounds model answers in retrieved documents: relevant chunks are fetched from a vector index and injected into the prompt, reducing hallucination. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prompt_engineering and https://mastra.ai/docs/rag

input.query: How does LibSQL differ from SQLite?

output.text: LibSQL differs from SQLite as a fork that adds replication, embedded replicas, and multiple API-compatible distributions, keeping SQLite's semantics while scaling reads. Sources: https://tour.libsql.com and https://github.com/tursodatabase/libsql

input.query: What are embedding models used for?

output.text: Embedding models turn text into dense vectors so semantically similar strings land close together, powering semantic search, clustering, recall, and classification. Sources: https://mastra.ai/docs and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Word_embedding

input.query: Summarize the CAP theorem in distributed systems

output.text: The CAP theorem states a distributed system cannot simultaneously guarantee consistency, availability, and partition tolerance — during a network partition you trade consistency for availability or the reverse. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAP_theorem

input.query: What is OpenTelemetry and why use it with AI agents?

output.text: OpenTelemetry provides vendor-neutral traces and metrics; with AI agents it gives observability of LLM calls, tool invocations, and token cost so regressions and hallucination loops become visible. Sources: https://opentelemetry.io/docs and https://mastra.ai/docs/observability

Vertical slice architecture organizes code by feature end-to-end (UI, domain, data together in one folder) instead of by technical layer, so each slice is independently understandable and removable. Sources: https://jeremydmiller.com vertical slicing article

LLM-as-a-judge evaluation uses a capable model to score another model's output against explicit criteria such as relevancy, faithfulness, and hallucination, approximating human review at scale. Sources: https://mastra.ai/docs/evals and https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685
